source: ICNF, Arvoredo de Interesse Publico (Portugal's national register of trees of public interest)
licence_proof: Sem restricoes. A utilizacao ou divulgacao deste conjunto de dados geograficos requer sempre a indicacao expressa da sua proveniencia e autoria: ICNF. (https://geocatalogo.icnf.pt/metadados/arv_class.html)
scope: Complete national register, all 18 mainland districts. The earlier import held only 124 entries because the fetch was scoped to Lisboa, Porto and Sintra; the other 431 sat behind the same endpoint under the same licence.
caveat: Four things a run must know before using this. (1) girth_m and height_m are METRES: the previous import labelled the girth column girth_cm, which made a 2.84 metre trunk read as under three centimetres. (2) age_register is the age at last measurement, not today; 79 entries were last measured before 2005. (3) Fourteen register ages are implausible on their face, including a 4,590-year chestnut at Vinhais and a 3,350-year olive at Abrantes. They are register-claimed and would trip hard rule 8 if repeated; treat any age here as a lead to verify, never as a published figure. (4) There is no vitality field anywhere in this register, so nothing in it evidences that a given tree still stands.
